newsitem.title: CANADA: Repap slips on Avenor merger doubts.
newsitem.headline: Repap slips on Avenor merger doubts.

text.p: Shares of Repap Enterprises Inc slipped further on Friday on growing doubts that a proposed C$3.3 billion takeover by Avenor Inc will proceed, analysts said.
By late afternoon, Repap shares were down 0.40 on the Toronto Stock Exchange to 2.14, on a volume of more than one million shares, after dipping to 2.10 earlier in the day.
Analysts said the share price decline is a further indication that the market doubts Avenor shareholders will approve on March 12 Avenor's all-stock offer for Repap.
"My feeling is that Avenor is going to walk away from this thing completely," Sam Magid, analyst at Salman Partners, of Vancouver.
Avenor's, offer, made December 18, is to exchange one of its common shares for 4.25 Repap shares, a transaction that at December 18 stock prices valued Repap shares at C$5 each.
On the TSE Friday afternoon, Avenor shares were up 1.15 to 21.50 on a volume of more than 600,000 shares, trading at more than 10 times Repap's stock.
In the offer, Avenor also would take over Repap's C$2.4 billion of debt.

In the offering circular on the bid, Avenor has said it would seek to sell certain Avenor and Repap assets for gross proceeds of about C$850 million to lower an estimated C$3.2 billion of debt the merged companies would carry.

Analysts said that aside from significantly lowering effective transaction price of the all-stock offer, Avenor needs to sway its shareholders to the bid by providing assurances that it can quickly sell the assets.

Those assets include Avenor's Gold River pulp mill, its 53 percent interest in Pacific Forest Products Ltd, Repap's British Columbia operations, including its Skeena pulp mill, and Repap's Allcell pulp mill, a now closed experimental facility in New Brunswick.
"Avenor has got to crank up the ratio to about 8-to-1 and have sold off Pacific Forest Products, the Alcell pulp mill and Skeena before the acquisition closing," said analyst Magid.
"Then maybe the street would give it a shot," he said.
